We have spectrum peaks from m/z 276.07 with decreasing intensities. Need to identify elements definitively based on isotope distribution patterns visible.

We need to compare observed isotopic pattern: main peak at 276.0666 intensity 100, then M+1 at 277.0697 intensity ~16% of base, M+2 at 278.0640 intensity ~33.6% (higher than M+1), M+3 at 279.0669 intensity ~5.27%, M+4 at 280.0694 intensity ~0.53%, etc.

Which elements produce characteristic patterns? Chlorine: two isotopes 35Cl (75.8%) and 37Cl (24.2%) gives M+2 about 1/3 of M (approx 0.33). Ratio M+2/M ~0.33. Here M+2 is 33.6% of base, close to chlorine pattern. Also chlorine gives M+2 peak at ~1/3 intensity, and M+4 negligible. But we also see M+1 at 16% which could be due to carbon (13C) ~1.1% per carbon; many carbons give M+1. But chlorine's M+2 is distinctive.

Bromine: isotopes 79Br (50.7%) and 81Br (49.3%) gives M+2 about equal intensity to M. Not observed.

Sulfur: 32S (95%) and 34S (4.2%) gives M+2 about 4% of base, not 33%.

Oxygen: 18O 0.2% gives small M+2.

Thus chlorine is definitively present. Also carbon is likely present because M+1 is 16% suggests many carbons (approx 14 carbons would give ~15%). But carbon isotopic pattern is not definitive because many elements contribute to M+1. However we can be confident that chlorine is present.

Any other element with distinctive pattern? Maybe bromine not present. No strong M+2 ~1:1.

Thus answer list: ["Cl"].

Check if any other element can be definitively identified: The presence of chlorine is clear. Could also identify carbon? Not definitive because M+1 could be from many elements. So only chlorine.

Return list format ['Cl'].
